pages.text: Zulaiha and Nsoh watered the school garden every morning. “How does a plant drink?” asked Nsoh. “It has no mouth.” “Let us find out,” said Zulaiha.
sentences: Zulaiha and Nsoh watered the school garden every morning.
“How does a plant drink?” asked Nsoh.
“It has no mouth.” “Let us find out,” said Zulaiha.
pages.alt: In a lush Ghanaian school garden, Zulaiha and Nsoh water leafy green vegetable beds with a watering can under morning sunshine.

pages.text: Their teacher helped them set up a test. They half-filled a clear glass jar with water and added a few drops of safe red food colouring. Next, they placed the freshly trimmed stem of a white flower into the red water.
sentences: Their teacher helped them set up a test.
They half-filled a clear glass jar with water and added a few drops of safe red food colouring.
Next, they placed the freshly trimmed stem of a white flower into the red water.
pages.alt: On a wooden classroom table, Zulaiha and Nsoh watch as their teacher places a leafy white flower stem into a clear jar of bright red water.

pages.text: They waited patiently. After one hour, nothing seemed different. After a few hours, however, the pale edges of the white petals turned soft pink. “It is working!” whispered Zulaiha.
sentences: They waited patiently.
After one hour, nothing seemed different.
After a few hours, however, the pale edges of the white petals turned soft pink.
“It is working!” whispered Zulaiha.
pages.alt: Close view of the clear jar of red water on the sunny windowsill as the white flower petals show delicate pink edges while Zulaiha and Nsoh peer closely.

pages.text: By the next morning, the petals were bright rosy red. Their teacher carefully cut across the bottom of the stem. “Look at the tiny red dots,” she said. “Those are narrow tubes inside the stem. The coloured water climbed right up through them.”
sentences: By the next morning, the petals were bright rosy red.
Their teacher carefully cut across the bottom of the stem.
“Look at the tiny red dots,” she said.
“Those are narrow tubes inside the stem.
The coloured water climbed right up through them.”
pages.alt: Their teacher holding the freshly cut green stem end to show tiny red dots inside while the rosy red flower rests beside Zulaiha and Nsoh.

pages.text: “In the soil, a plant’s roots take in water,” explained their teacher. “Then the stem carries that water all the way up to the leaves and flowers so the plant can live and grow.”
sentences: “In the soil, a plant’s roots take in water,” explained their teacher.
“Then the stem carries that water all the way up to the leaves and flowers so the plant can live and grow.”
pages.alt: Out in the school garden, the teacher kneels beside a healthy flowering plant and traces her finger from the damp soil at its base up the green stem to the blossoms.

pages.text: Zulaiha and Nsoh watered the garden with a clear new purpose. “Pour water near the roots, not high on the leaves,” said Nsoh. “And never waste a drop,” added Zulaiha. When they finished, both children washed their hands with soap.
sentences: Zulaiha and Nsoh watered the garden with a clear new purpose.
“Pour water near the roots, not high on the leaves,” said Nsoh.
“And never waste a drop,” added Zulaiha.
When they finished, both children washed their hands with soap.
pages.alt: Nsoh carefully pouring water right at the soil base of garden plants while Zulaiha washes her hands at a clean outdoor tap nearby.

activities.question: What carried the coloured water up to the petals?
What is the job of a plant’s roots?
options: Take in water from the soil

activities.prompt: Put the plant’s drinking journey in order.
items: The roots take in water from the soil.
The stem carries the water upward.
The leaves and flowers receive water.
The plant lives and grows strong.

activities.definition: The parts of a plant that grow under the soil and take in water.

glossary.definition: The main stalk of a plant that carries water up from the roots.
The parts of a plant that grow under the soil and take in water.
The soft coloured outer parts of a flower.
